lens: BENEFIT: the best honest case for what each family would buy on W1 (CLAUDE.md length) and L2 (context budget, compaction), with strict evidence scoring. Shared experiment E1 (the CLAUDE.md ablation, referenced below): 10 frozen probe tasks, each needing one CLAUDE.md invariant (next migration slot, a new outbox kind, comparing a shared secret, deploying from backend/, the eas.json DSN, the dispatcher cursor, a bill-freeze resubmit, money units, a new slice edge, droppable pings). Each task runs in one fresh Sonnet session per arm. An Opus judge, blind to the arm, scores whether the agent's plan cites and obeys the invariant. The result is also checked against the knowledge-store gating (KS-7/D11), which these families mostly cannot pre-empt.

reviews.measurement: E1 with two arms: the current CLAUDE.md, and the same text with task-specific sections wrapped in <important if> blocks, nothing deleted. Adopt the wrapped file only if it scores at least as well as the current one on all 10 probe tasks and better on at least 2.
reviews.reason: This is the only W1 lever that removes no content, so the knowledge-store gating ('a trim takes knowledge from sessions that never look up') does not apply. It needs an ablation because the only evidence is HumanLayer's unmeasured 'noticeably better'.

reviews.measurement: Rerun 8 committed Opus xhigh skeptic or reviewer briefs at medium (keep Opus), each against the commit its brief named, and diff the verdicts (CONFIRMED/REFUTED/UNVERIFIABLE) plus the traced path. Pass if at least 7 of 8 verdicts agree AND medium misses no CONFIRMED P0. Then move non-invariant verifiers to medium or high and keep xhigh for P0 and invariant skeptics. Otherwise keep xhigh. Run it only if G4-F203 shows verifier spend at 20% or more.
reviews.reason: This is the cheapest honest test of L1: about 8 Opus runs on a labeled set we already hold. SlopCodeBench's medium-versus-xhigh result is measured on a different task type, so it cannot be adopted untested.
